newsitem.title: SOMALIA: At least 10 killed in attacks in Somali capital.
newsitem.headline: At least 10 killed in attacks in Somali capital.

text.p: At least 10 people were killed and nine wounded in a string of attacks and clashes in the Somali capital on Friday and early on Saturday, witnesses said.
An upsurge in violence had been widely expected in Mogadishu as rival factions jostle for power during Kenyan-sponsored Somali peace talks in Nairobi.

Witnesses said six people were killed and four wounded when a 120 mm mortar bomb slammed into a vehicle on Friday carrying passengers in Medina district, which is blockaded by Hussein Aideed's forces.
One person was killed and two were wounded when a land mine exploded in a house on the frontline dividing militiamen loyal to Medina faction leader Musa Sudi Yalahow and others loyal to Aideed.
Another person was killed and two were wounded in a clash on the Green Line battle zone dividing south and north Mogadishu between Aideed's fighters and forces loyal to Ali Mahdi Mohamed.
Early on Saturday, two supporters of faction leader Ali Hassan Osman Atto were gunned down and killed in south Mogadishu by unidentified gunmen, who also wounded one other person.
Residents said all factions were plainly on high alert with "technicals", four-wheel-drive battlewagons bristling with weapons and gunmen, prowling the streets every night.
Most faction leaders including Aideed, Ali Mahdi and Osman Atto arrived in Nairobi this week for exploratory peace talks sponsored by Kenyan President Daniel arap Moi.
They are the first inter-factional talks involving Aideed, a 34-year-old former U.S. marine who took over from his father Mohamed Farah Aideed after his death in Mogadishu on August 1.
Aideed, like his father, was elected president of Somalia by supporters and heads a government. But it has not received much international recognition and is rejected by Ali Mahdi and other leaders.
South Mogadishu has been hit in the past several weeks by a series of assassinations which Somali experts say are part of a vendetta between groups to avenge Mohamed Farah Aideed's death.

Moi has been closely involved in several earlier diplomatic initiatives to build peace in Somalia, including a face-to-face reconciliation meeting in Nairobi between Ali Mahdi and Mohamed Farah Aideed in 1994, but they all failed to stop the fighting.
